outcome.headline: Spain edged England 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final, dominating possession and shot volume behind a dynamic front line that carried the game to a late winner.

standout_performers.reason: Led Spain's buildup with 48 completed passes in the first half alone and repeatedly launched progressive line-breaking passes and carries from left centre-back, including a 56-yard progressive pass in the 46th minute.

tactics.prose:
Both sides set up in a 4-2-3-1, with Spain building around Rodri and Fabián Ruiz as the double pivot behind Dani Olmo, and England mirroring the shape with Declan Rice and Kobbie Mainoo screening in front of the back four and Foden operating centrally behind Kane. Spain's on-ball centroid (62.2, 41.4) sat marginally deeper and more central than England's (69.8, 39.2), whose average shape pushed further up the pitch, consistent with England's higher defensive block and deeper territorial occupation into Spain's half. Spain's first-half hull stretched from Unai Simón in the defensive third out to a front line featuring Cucurella, Morata and Lamine Yamal high and wide, showing a possession structure built through the back three of Le Normand, Laporte and the full-backs before progressing into the front four. England's own hull in the opening period ran from Pickford through Stones and Guehi out to Kane and the front line, with Walker pushed high and central as an auxiliary presence alongside Mainoo and Foden.

Spain's passing network in the first period was dominated by the central defensive axis: Le Normand and Laporte combined 31 times between them, and Rodri and Carvajal both featured as heavy-volume nodes (29 and 36 passes respectively), indicating build-up circulated through the back line and the right side before reaching Fabián Ruiz, Nico Williams and Morata further forward. England's opening-period hub was similarly centred on their back three plus Rice, with Stones-Pickford (8), Rice-Bellingham (8) and Walker-Stones (7) the busiest connections, while Saka and Foden linked repeatedly with Walker and Mainoo down the right, showing England's progression skewed toward that side.

Spain made four changes across the second half and stoppage time — Zubimendi for Rodri at the interval, Oyarzabal for Morata just after the hour, Nacho for Le Normand late on, and Merino for Lamine Yamal in the closing minutes — while retaining the 4-2-3-1 shape throughout until a brief 89th-minute window. England altered personnel three times (Watkins for Kane, Palmer for Mainoo, Toney for Foden) and shifted formation late, moving from 4-2-3-1 to a 4-1-2-1-2 in the 89th minute with Rice as the lone holding midfielder and Bellingham and Saka pushed into a flat central midfield two alongside Toney and Watkins up front. In the 69'–89' window, England's passing hub shifted toward Bellingham and the newly introduced Cole Palmer, who combined four times, with Saka and Walker still prominent down the right; Spain's late-window network became sparser and more fragmented, with Fabián Ruiz, Nacho and Daniel Olmo forming a reduced central relay as the side management-heavy closing periods produced fewer sustained combinations for either team.
